summary: Listed as a verified fire tower point in Ontario's open tower layer; no other source reached describes its history, staffing or present site.

evidence.supports: The layer lists a Loughrin Fire Tower
Point at about 46.5401 N, 80.5275 W (longitude first in the source)
Location placed within 50 metres of the site
The layer classes it as a fire tower
Most Ontario towers were erected between the 1920s and the 1950s, when forest fire protection was at its height
evidence.quote: Most of the towers were erected between the 1920's and the 1950's when forest fire protection was in it's heyday.

evidence.supports: The site is a personal history site
evidence.quote: I decided I would produce a website to preserve the history of our fire tower lookouts and the towermen that worked them.

evidence.supports: By the 1960s the towers were used less and less as aerial spotting and firefighting took over
evidence.quote: As the 1960's progressed the towers were in use less and less as aerial fire spotting and fire fighting crews took over.

evidence.supports: A decision was made to have many towers destroyed
evidence.quote: The decision then went through to have many destroyed.

sources.title: Fire tower points, Land Information Ontario open data
Ontario's Fire Tower Lookouts
sources.publisher: Ontario's Fire Tower Lookouts (personal history site)

notes_for_editor: The brief gives no local_unit for this tower, so the story names only Ontario. The brief's source page (geohub.lio.gov.on.ca/datasets/mnrf::tower) has no record text in the cache, so the cited source is the LIO query response it points to, which is cached under the URL in sources[0]. The record has no height, build year, status or agency fields. The layer's GENERAL_COMMENTS field says only that the location came from an 'AFFM Tower dataset', and the story does not expand that acronym because no source explains it. Two searches for Loughrin and reads of the Firelookout.ca and Ontario hobby-site lists turned up nothing further. The story sits at the 120-word floor because the evidence is thin; it was not padded beyond what the sources support.
